panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Low-power H&E of patient breast cores showing inflammation centered on ducts and lobules with stromal sparing, the classic lobulocentric pattern of granulomatous lobular mastitis; article title and in-text context confirm IGM. B: H&E at 10x shows periductal granulomatous inflammation with multinucleated giant cells, a characteristic histologic manifestation of idiopathic granulomatous mastitis in a human patient breast core. C: Perilobular inflammation at 10x directly demonstrates granulomatous lobulitis, the defining lobulocentric granulomatous pattern of granulomatous lobular mastitis in patient breast tissue. D: High-power H&E at 40x shows granulomas involving ducts with multinucleated giant cells, the textbook histologic hallmark of idiopathic granulomatous mastitis in a human patient biopsy.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels ((a), (b)). (a): H&E core-biopsy panel at 100x showing an epithelioid granuloma centered on breast lobular acini with lymphocytic infiltrate, matching the lobulocentric non-caseating granuloma of idiopathic granulomatous mastitis; in-text describes neutrophilic microabscesses in the figure. Real human patient histology, disease attribution clear from caption and article title. (b): High-power H&E (400x) view of the same core-biopsy granuloma showing epithelioid histiocytes with lymphocytes and neutrophils, consistent with the epithelioid granuloma and neutrophilic microabscesses described for idiopathic granulomatous lobular mastitis. Disease attribution is strongly supported by the disease-focused title and in-text biopsy-confirmed context. Confidence is moderate rather than high because the caption describes a non-specific 'area of abnormal echogenicity' and explicitly notes no discrete mass or collection, so the exact 'tubular lesion with sinus tract' morphology is only partially supported (visual hypoechoic area). No skin, ethnicity, or age is assessable/stated, and this is not an AS case, so those fields are null/unknown.

panels.rationale: Single-panel H&E cytology/histopathology image of aspirated breast cystic fluid from a patient in an idiopathic granulomatous mastitis case report. The caption and in-text describe predominantly neutrophils (polymorphonuclear cells) in a hemorrhagic background with negative bacterial culture after 48 hours, representing sterile acute suppurative neutrophilic inflammation consistent with the neutrophilic microabscess component of granulomatous lobular mastitis. No granulomas are visible in this field, so disease attribution rests on the disease-focused article title together with the specific captioned neutrophilic manifestation; the caption's 'acute mastitis' framing and absence of granulomatous inflammation lower confidence. Blue arrow annotation is present.
